title: CoreWeave CEO Blames Rivals After Bonds Hit Record 15% Yield

tickers.name: CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock
Nebius Group N.V. Class A Ordinary Shares

summary:
The shares of AI cloud provider CoreWeave plummeted on Wednesday, marking the company as one of the worst-performing stocks on the Nasdaq 100 index. The equity drop of nearly 15% coincided with unsecured bonds hitting a record 15% yield and credit default swaps expanding to 1,050 basis points. CEO Michael Intrator defended the firm's stability in an email seen by Bloomberg, stating that the weakness of rivals is "bleeding into" the market narrative and that the company's backlog more than supports its debt obligations.

The market volatility follows reports that CoreWeave carries roughly $52B in debt and leases against a $104B backlog, with net interest costs of $640M last quarter consuming about 25% of its revenue. The sell-off hit other neocloud players, including Nebius, which saw shares fall 9.7%. While credit markets price in higher risk for these providers, analysts note that Nvidia relies on CoreWeave's growth to maintain leverage against hyperscalers like Microsoft and Amazon.

selectedTweets.text:
Everyone needs to STOP worrying so much about this neocloud selloff.

I think people are forgetting just how important companies like $CRWV and $NBIS are to the entire AI ecosystem, especially $NVDA. And remember what Jensen Huang announced just TWO months ago? Nvidia partnered with BlackRock, Blackstone, Goldman Sachs, Apollo, Brookfield, and KKR to help mobilize over $500 BILLION in financing for AI infrastructure. Think about what that actually means. Jensen understands that the biggest bottleneck in AI isn't necessarily demand anymore, it's getting enough capital, power, and infrastructure to actually meet that demand.

Also, Jensen NEEDS these neoclouds to succeed because they give Nvidia leverage against the hyperscalers. Companies like $MSFT, $AMZN, and $GOOGL are developing their own custom AI chips to reduce their dependence on Nvidia over time. And that's exactly why neoclouds are so important. Companies like CoreWeave and Nebius are building enormous amounts of GPU infrastructure centered around Nvidia's technology. They give AI companies another place to access compute without having to rely entirely on the traditional hyperscalers. The stronger these neoclouds become, the more alternatives customers have and the less dependent Nvidia becomes on a handful of hyperscalers controlling AI infrastructure spending.

Now imagine what happens if these neoclouds suddenly struggle to finance their expansion, which is exactly what we're starting to see with  $CRWV. CoreWeave's bond yields just surged to over 15%, which is a warning sign. For context, these bonds were issued at a 9.625% yield just four months ago and now investors are demanding significantly higher returns to hold that debt. Essentially, the bond market is telling us that investors are becoming increasingly concerned about CoreWeave's financial risks, which could make future borrowing a lot more expensive. And that's a massive problem for $NVDA because these companies are buying billions of dollars worth of GPUs and helping expand the market for Nvidia's technology. This is why I believe Jensen will step in to support strategically important partners like CoreWeave if financing conditions become difficult. Nvidia has already demonstrated that it's willing to put capital behind this ecosystem. I'm not saying Jensen will bail out every neocloud, but I find it very hard to believe he'll just sit back and watch one of his most important customers struggle to finance its expansion, especially when Nvidia needs these companies to compete against the hyperscalers.

selectedTweets.text:
🦔CoreWeave stock fell about 13% Wednesday after its bonds due in 2032 traded at a record 14.5% yield. CoreWeave sold those bonds in June at 9.625%, so in four months the cost of lending to it without collateral jumped about five points. Venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya posted the yield chart as a warning about a private credit bubble around AI.

My Take
I've been saying that the AI bubble lives in the debt more than the demand, and CoreWeave is an example. It raised more than $35 billion this year, carries about $52 billion in debt and leases, and paid $640 million in net interest last quarter, roughly a quarter of its revenue. The $104 billion backlog sounds great, but a backlog doesn’t cover interest until the data centers get built and the customers pay.

Palihapitiya’s numbers show private lenders charge AI borrowers almost the same spread as everyone else, 6.2 points versus 6.1. I think the bond market just repriced that risk for them. My guess is CoreWeave’s next raise costs more, comes backed by chips, or dilutes shareholders, and Nebius and the other AI cloud companies face the same questions. If you own a private credit fund, find out how much AI and software debt it holds, because those loans don’t get repriced every day the way CoreWeave’s bonds do.

Hedgie🤗
